title: Cornish Game Hen, Roasted, Skin Eaten

content.title: About
content.content: The Cornish game hen is a small domestic bird, typically weighing 400–600 g. When roasted, the skin stays crisp and edible, while the meat remains tender and flavorful. It is often served whole in restaurants and at festive meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cornish game hens were developed in England in the 19th century as ornamental bantam chickens.
They reach only about 30 cm in height, making them quick to cook.
The meat is considered more tender than that of standard chickens because of its high protein and low fat content.
Traditionally they are roasted whole, frequently stuffed with herbs, lemon, and garlic.
In the United States the bird is commonly called “Cornish game hen,” although it is not a game bird.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving of roasted cornish hen provides about 24 g of high‑quality protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other poultry, the cornish hen contains relatively little fat, especially when the skin is kept crisp but not over‑fried.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat is a good source of niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Does not cause a rapid spike in blood sugar, making it suitable for those monitoring glycemic response.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bird proteins.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: As with any meat, it should be cooked to an internal temperature of 74 °C to prevent salmonella.

items.title: High sodium in marinades
items.content: If the bird is pre‑marinated in salty solutions, sodium intake should be considered.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted cornish hen is served whole, then cut into portions. The skin is edible and adds a pleasant crunch. The meat pairs well with herbs, lemon, garlic, and sauces such as butter‑based gravies or yogurt‑based dressings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh meat should be kept in the refrigerator at +2–4 °C for no more than 2 days. Frozen meat can be stored at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking, never at room temperature.
